body:
Both sequences and column aliases are restricted by `NAMEDATALEN` right?

This is a problem that also exists in Oracle, which is limited to 32 characters for identifiers.

Really there needs to be a global solution for shortening identifiers, either through the naming strategy where users could do a more advanced truncation (e.g. remove vowels first, shorten common phrases) or a common hashing system.

<!--

  for general support or questions.  Instead, check the "Support" Documentation
  on the best places to ask questions!

  https://github.com/typeorm/typeorm/blob/master/docs/support.md
-->

## Issue Description
When I was submitting https://github.com/typeorm/typeorm/issues/7106 I reviewed the existing code that resolved the similar issue https://github.com/typeorm/typeorm/issues/3118, in PR https://github.com/typeorm/typeorm/pull/3514 , specifically https://github.com/typeorm/typeorm/blob/c4a36da62593469436b074873eba186f0f8b990d/src/driver/DriverUtils.ts#L51 
and noticed that this has a corner case:
The check is defined in terms of UTF-16 bytes (since this is what `.length` returns). However PostgreSQL defines the limit in terms of UTF-8 bytes. MySQL defines the limit in terms of characters. Number of UTF-16 bytes is not necessarily = the number of characters (MySQL case), nor is it necessarily = the number of UTF-8 bytes, depending on what characters are used. 

I am taking a strong guess that this second one applies to all databases where `maxAliasLength && maxAliasLength > 0`.

### Expected Behaviour

Checks should be against the actual limit of the database.

### Actual Behaviour

Check is against a UTF-16 limit. Will break where the length in UTF-16 bytes differs from the number of characters or UTF-8 bytes or however the limit is defined by the database.

### Steps to Reproduce

<!--
  Your bug will be investigated much faster if we can run your code and it doesn't
  have dependencies other than TypeORM. Issues without reproduction steps or
  code examples may be closed as not actionable.

  Please try to provide a Minimal, Complete, and Verifiable example.
  http://stackoverflow.com/help/mcve
-->

Use a name near the limit where the UTF-16 length differs substantially from the length in characters / length in UTF-8 bytes (/ other?)

### My Environment

  For example: Electron, React Native, or NestJS.
-->

| Node.js version     | v15.2.1 | <!-- run `node -v` to obtain this -->
| Typescript version  | v4.0.2 | <!-- run `npm list typescript` to obtain this -->
| TypeORM version     | v0.2.29 | <!-- run `npm list typeorm` to obtain this -->


### Additional Context

https://www.postgresql.org/docs/13/limits.html
https://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/8.0/en/identifier-length.html 

### Relevant Database Driver(s)

<!--
  Please include the relevant database drivers to your issue.

  Please include an `x` inside the brackets like so:

  - [x] `cordova`
  - [ ] `expo`

-->

body:
Yes all identifiers are restricted, in the case of PostgreSQL this is by NAMEDATALEN.

There is a global solution introduced in https://github.com/typeorm/typeorm/pull/3514 where table names and column aliases are checked (although imperfectly in corner cases #7107) and shortened by a [function](https://github.com/typeorm/typeorm/blob/c4a36da62593469436b074873eba186f0f8b990d/src/util/StringUtils.ts#L76) with some options / you could always change it. For reference Oracle (older versions) are 30 bytes, not 32 characters. https://docs.oracle.com/database/121/SQLRF/sql_elements008.htm#SQLRF51129

Reading through the code a bit more, only PostgreSQL and CockroachDB drivers create sequences and (in the case of CockroachDB, potentially) suffer from this bug. I will submit a bug fix (ignoring #7107) for those.

Ah I see, I was aware of that function but didn't know there was a `StringUtils.shorten()` before the hashing that was introduced in #5227. Unfortunately it still isn't applied in all circumstances, so some work is needed there anyway.

Ideally we could reintroduce `shorten()` along with the suggestion of having an alias map, as per https://github.com/typeorm/typeorm/pull/5227#issuecomment-568044039. There might be some differentiation between permanent identifiers like the sequence name, and temporary aliases per query.

Either way quick fix sounds like a good idea for now.

On further investigation it's a little bit more tricky, and way more specific, than I first thought. The problem first starts when TypeORM uses the default PostgreSQL sequence name. PostgreSQL is smart enough to truncate, however it uses its own, different algorithm again to `StringUtils.shorten()`. I have no idea if CockroachDB suffers from the same issue, or how it resolves with without more research but I will look into it, as it's the only other TypeORM driver where a sequence name is generated.

Bumps [typeorm](https://github.com/typeorm/typeorm) from 0.2.29 to 0.2.31.
Changelog

Sourced from typeorm's changelog.

0.2.31 (2021-02-08)

Bug Fixes

  • append condition to STI child entity join (#7339) (68bb82e)
  • avoid regex lookbehind for compatibility (#7270) (063d27f), closes #7026
  • cache from ENV - add ioredis support (#7332) (5e2117c)
  • datetime2 rounding in mssql (#7264) (4711a71), closes #3202
  • escape columns in InsertQueryBuilder.orUpdate (#6316) (ab56e07)
  • incorrect postgres uuid type in PrimaryGeneratedColumnType (#7298) (2758502)
  • MariaDB VIRTUAL + [NOT NULL|NULL] error (#7022) (82f2b75), closes #2691
  • reject nullable primary key columns (#7001) (cdace6e)
  • resolve issue with find with relations returns soft-deleted entities (#7296) (d7cb338), closes #6265
  • save does not return id, save does not return generated (#7336) (01a6aee)

Features

  • enable explicitly inserting IDENTITY values into mssql (#6199) (4abbd46), closes #2199
  • export all errors (#7006) (56300d8)
  • option to disable foreign keys creation (#7277) (cb17b95), closes #3120 #3120
  • support maxdecimaldigits option by geometry type (#7166) (d749008)
  • useUTC connection option for oracle and postgres (#7295) (e06a442)

BREAKING CHANGES

  • passing ColumnOptions to @PrimaryColumn does not function anymore. One must use PrimaryColumnOptions instead.
  • minor breaking change on "conflict*" options - column names used are now automatically escaped.
